name: Facet
text: Choose a dark theme by default with a one-click toggle to light mode. It reduces eye strain in low-light settings and keeps visuals crisp, which matters for long sessions. The trade-off is that some users prefer light themes for readability in bright rooms—accept that by making the toggle instant and prominent.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes don’t just strain eyes—they bury errors in shadows and mute critical data, turning "crisp visuals" into a liability when users miss red flags. A better alternative: default to a high-contrast light theme with a dark mode toggle, since glare is easier to ignore than hidden failures. Settle it with A/B tests measuring error detection rates and user-reported misses in both modes.
